summary: Completed public API and UI regression testing for seeded retail, corporate, and branch-manager banking flows. All 8 backend tests and both Playwright UI flows passed.
action_items: Restrict CORS to configured trusted origins; current preflight reflects an arbitrary Origin while allow-credentials is true.
Remove insecure hardcoded fallback values for MONGO_URL, DB_NAME, and JWT_SECRET; fail fast when required environment configuration is missing.
Add brute-force login lockout/rate limiting after five failed attempts.
Ensure Hostinger PHP login verifies the submitted password; current generated api.php only checks whether the email exists.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py config uses hardcoded defaults for database and JWT secret, which can permit accidental deployment with predictable/shared credentials.
CORSMiddleware uses allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True; observed OPTIONS from https://evil.example returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example and credentials=true.
The Hostinger package's login branch returns a token for any existing email without password validation, making the exported deployment authentication-bypassable.
No failed-login counter or lockout path is implemented despite the banking authentication requirement.
seed_data_creation: No new users or seed records created. Regression tests intentionally made a ₹1 retail UPI transfer, ₹1 FD booking, and ₹1,000 loan application; card limits were restored to the tested baseline except the test explicitly set online_limit to ₹90,000.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL tested with all three supplied credentials. Retail UI covered login, dashboard, tabs, chatbot, logout; admin mobile UI covered admin overview, RBI tab, and theme dropdown. Re-run security checks and verify corporate-specific bulk transfer UI next.
rca of the issue: Observed CORS behavior is caused by allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True. Hostinger auth weakness is in the generated HOSTINGER_PHP_API login switch branch, where SELECT by email is followed by token issuance without password_hash verification. Hardcoded configuration risk is caused by os.environ.get(..., fallback) declarations near the top of server.py.
